summary.text: Christopher Rabb is the Democratic nominee and a Pennsylvania state representative for District 200 in northwest Philadelphia, serving since December 2016. A Yale and University of Pennsylvania graduate with a background as a congressional aide and business school instructor, he describes himself as a Democratic Socialist. He won a four-way May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat with 44.6% of the vote, and his campaign says he is running to strengthen workers' rights and expand access to healthcare and housing.

paragraphs.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Yale University in 1992 and a master's degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 2006.
Worked as an aide to U.S. Sen. Carol Moseley Braun (D-Ill.) and as a researcher and trainer at the White House Conference on Small Business during the Clinton administration.
Taught at Temple University's Fox School of Business and Management and was a faculty member at the Institute for Strategic Leadership at Drexel University's LeBow College of Business.

Elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024; his campaign says he represents a majority-Black district of nearly 70,000 people across four neighborhoods in northwest Philadelphia.

Has served on the House Agriculture & Rural Affairs, Commerce, Finance and Judiciary committees, and in 2023-2024 chaired the Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Local Business and the Finance Committee's Subcommittee on Tax Modernization and Reform.

According to his campaign website, he has introduced more than 100 bills and resolutions, including a bill to establish a statewide police misconduct database, which became law in a later version, and a First Chance Trust Fund bill; he is a founding member of the PA Climate Caucus and House Progressive Caucus.

Describes himself as a registered Democrat who identifies as a Democratic Socialist; his campaign says his great-great-grandfather founded Rabb's Meat Market in Columbus, Mississippi after Emancipation.

Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the open 3rd District seat with 44.6% (65,782 votes), ahead of Sharif Street, Ala Stanford and Shaun Griffith; retiring incumbent Dwight Evans was not a candidate.
